text:
Stephen Halliday is a fourth-round pick turning into a real NHL player in front of us. The Senators forward is 24, playing 11:27 a night after 8:31 last season, and on the ice for 47% of Ottawa's power-play chances, up from 33%. Seven of his 11 points have come on the man advantage, including a power-play goal against Los Angeles on Nov. 22.

Our numbers call it a breakout, and they think he's been unlucky with it. His own chances are up to 1.10 expected goals per 60 from 0.75, and Ottawa has scored 5.5 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. His 2.22 points per 60 sit right in the middle of our talent range, so this isn't a hot streak dressed up as progress.

The caveat is five on five, where the Senators do about six points worse by expected-goal share with him out there than without. That's the part to watch as Ottawa keeps winning (seven of its last ten). A power-play regular who came through Belleville the long way has a job. Keeping it means holding up at even strength.
headline: Halliday has earned the bigger role
